title: Open product decisions
objective: Resolve the product questions that gate later roadmap phases, recording each answer in docs/decisions.md and the affected specification.
context_summary: Accepted decisions live in docs/decisions.md. These tasks cover storage and backup, the first external module use case, performance workloads and provisional budgets, Presence/mixer/vignette defaults, reconciliation of the owner's GPU decisions with remaining implementation and qualification, UI themes defaults, and Lightroom implementation authorization. The catalog, presets and Tone curve defaults remain proposals in their designs; no additional decision task is introduced.

tasks.description: Research storage workflows and decide later catalog portability and backup behavior.
extra_context: Later product research on storage/backup/sidecars and broader photographer workflows. It does not gate the catalog history foundation or agreed manual Locate.

The current catalog uses WAL; a consistent backup must account for its live WAL and derived-artifact directory as well as catalog rows. Manual Locate and the delivered missing-original workflow are not a backup or sync strategy.

tasks.description: Choose the first external module use case and user-visible enablement/recovery behavior.
extra_context: External module loading remains required, but the use case, runtime and user-facing lifecycle need a concrete decision.
The linked tool-module milestone is already selected and does not wait on external packaging or a marketplace.

GPU-first changes the processing-tool host boundary: a new image effect needs a CPU reference unit with exact fixtures and a module-owned WGSL program held within the declared tolerance by gpu-qualification. Without a GPU program the stack uses the named no-program reference fallback, including export; missing or disabled providers must still report affected edits rather than omit them. External GPU loading remains unimplemented and is not implied by the built-in program interface.

tasks.description: Prioritize performance workloads and settle user-visible responsiveness goals.
extra_context: Record workload priorities and measured native M4 conditions; proposed performance budgets require evidence and owner acceptance.
Speed and lazy subsection editing within a full catalog are owner priorities. Avoid assuming binary splitting saves memory or latency.

Already accepted, and not reopened here: the slider-to-presented-frame target of 16 ms p95 with 32 ms acceptable (docs/decisions.md, Basic adjustments and histogram), shared working-memory budgets as targets that pace work rather than limits (Rendering memory), and the owner's 150 ms bound for the hold-`\` compare that chose the second RAW development (Post-consolidation review).

Already decided: the 2 GiB GPU-preview budget and up to sixteen masked spatial layers (2026-10-03), and the tile worker's separate 2 GiB budget (2026-10-06). These application charges are not a total-memory guarantee; full-photo slots share a 1 GiB ceiling and native staging/device overhead remain unqualified. The settled-histogram workload now measures GPU counts over full-resolution tiles, held within the decided histogram tolerance of the reference.

The M4 throughput measurement of 2026-10-07 records slider, histogram, burst, memory and idle targets passing; launch (2.07 to 2.11 s) and uncached 24 MP open (1.21 to 1.25 s) miss provisional targets, about 0.45 s of each attributable to the host on both compared builds. Paint at 100% and trivial GPU export remain measured misses. The owner's 2026-10-07 attribution choice uses resources.read and the Performance section; it authorizes no new total-memory claim or unsupported performance result.

tasks.description: Refine the recorded defaults of the Presence, colour mixer and vignette proposals after reviewing the delivered work.
extra_context: Remaining recorded defaults: Presence as the section name for Texture, Clarity and Dehaze; colour before spatial before geometry before finish with the mixer after Basic; three property groups for the mixer; one luminance-neutral vignette style. These remain proposals after the owner's 2026-10-07 review.

Implementation was authorized on 2026-09-22 on the recorded defaults. A proposal is not a decision until the owner records it; until then the delivered behaviour follows the default and the design keeps calling it a proposal.

JPEG spatial precision was decided on 2026-09-30: 16-bit encoded hand-off between spatial frames and the next colour run or spatial unit, delivered with Detail (docs/design/presence-mixer-vignette.md).

The old full-resolution CPU spatial-draft and O(halo² × layers) point-sample proposals are superseded by GPU-first: spatial drags use the GPU at every zoom, with display-sized CPU proxy drags only without a usable GPU; every desktop pixel read uses a GPU tile or named reference fallback. A three-segment Air 2S sample measures 85.4 / 91.7 ms p50 / p95 warm. These renderer paths are decided, not remaining Presence product choices.

tasks.description: Reconcile the accepted GPU-first and GPU-preview defaults, softer budget-reduced motion at 100% now qualified and reported ungated, while keeping later GPU optimisation proposals distinct from delivered behaviour.
extra_context: Owner, 2026-10-07: current picture, sample and export class tolerances are accepted. Samples use the class statistics with no block statistic over scattered points, and equal the at-rest screen byte at 100%. Fast reduced-source motion below 100% reports differences against rest and reference; the at-rest gate remains strict. Softer budget-reduced motion at 100% is accepted subject to explicit qualification, which is not supplied by this decision.

The full gate of 2026-10-06 (55c42f38) measures 261 stacks and 1,044 at-rest cells within their limits; motion below 100% misses on 462 of 783 cells. That evidence measures the view plans named there, not every budget-reduced 100% stack/view. Neither this review nor product acceptance is new native qualification evidence.

Owner, 2026-10-07: the current displayed/updating counts cadence, GPU export with explicit reference option, reference fallback and whole-export restart, and owner work on the blocking pool are accepted. Current release-compilation behaviour, first-photograph warm-up, at-most-four per-pixel replays, and the host renderer for existing stored picks are accepted. The RAW sensor neutral picker actually reads a bounded 13×13 (169-site) patch on the owner thread; the owner accepted retaining that existing bounded read on 2026-10-07.

Owner, 2026-10-07: neutral-picker answers must name their renderer. Implemented: the host adds renderer {record, reason} to every module query that reads pixels, verified by headless reference and desktop GPU query tests.

Owner, 2026-10-07: the 150 ms linear-light dissolve, status-bar render timing with lasting fallback/reference notices and no canvas badge, shrinking scratch pool and current qualified mixed precision are accepted. Region padding, strip-ring evaluation, mask-bounded growth, per-link plane sizes and one-channel Detail remain unimplemented optimisation proposals with their own evidence requirements.

Already decided and not reopened: histogram/clipping tolerance; reference fallback with CPU-proxy drags without a usable GPU; software adapter not adopted; separate 2 GiB tile-worker budget; warm open's first GPU picture; exact light behind spatial layers at rest/export and the recorded motion stand-in. The owner keeps the current portability dependency and recommends small lavapipe functional journeys omitting large24/large60 and running all retained scenarios before failing the lane. This review changes no CI code and claims no passing hosted lane.

tasks.description: Decide the remaining UI themes questions: which Omarchy themes are bundled, the contrast floors and moving an imported theme's own ink, the Omarchy forms read, a Theme choice for the canvas background as its default, the Appearance tab, and whether following Omarchy's current theme or the system appearance is built next.
extra_context: The owner decided on 2026-10-05 (docs/decisions.md, UI themes) that themes, light ones included, replace dark only; that the surround stays neutral; that each theme keeps its own accent; and that a few popular Omarchy themes are bundled. Themes are implemented on the design's default for each remaining question, and each is a proposal until it is recorded here.

The recorded defaults: Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Catppuccin Latte, Gruvbox, Nord and Everforest bundled; floors of 7:1 for primary text, 4.5:1 for labels, secondary text and accent ink, and 3:1 for tertiary text, the accent and the error ink, with an imported theme's own text or accent moved to its floor and reported (6 of Omarchy's 22 built-in themes); Omarchy 4 and 3 palettes, light.mode and alacritty.toml read; a fourth canvas background choice, Theme, as its default, with Dark, Black and Grey kept as fixed greys; a Settings › Appearance tab for the theme list, the canvas background and interface size staying General rows; following Omarchy's current theme and the system appearance left for later.

tasks.description: Decide whether the Lightroom import and Lightroom alignment task plans are authorized for implementation; every design question of both is decided.
extra_context: Decided on 2026-10-06 and recorded in docs/decisions.md under Lightroom alignment and in AGENTS.md's seventh pillar: sliders follow Lightroom's responses (level B) for every supported setting, targeted algorithm changes (level C) past the A8 threshold, order by editing area, generated XMP with a manual round-trip, rendered outputs compared only, with no reverse engineering or Adobe code, the base rendering subtracted, earlier recipes refused, local validation with consent each run.

Owner, 2026-10-07: Lightroom supplies grid first tiles only, never a Develop large tile; an import is not undoable as a group. Calibrated RAW preset white-balance conversion belongs to alignment. The prohibition on Adobe-derived code and tables applies to new alignment work; the existing RAW importer isotemperature table gets a separate review. These scope answers do not authorize implementation of either plan.
